criteria.text: Calculates the long-stop date as 19 January 2027 (120 days after signing on 21 September 2026) and identifies that expected clearance on 2 February 2027 falls after it, recommending an extension.

Identifies that the board approval was given at a meeting with only 2 directors present when Article 11 requires a quorum of three, so the approval may be invalid, and recommends a fresh or ratifying resolution.
States that General Warranty claims must be notified by 14 June 2028 (18 months after Closing) and Fundamental Warranty claims by 14 December 2030 (48 months after Closing).

Identifies the threatened $2,750,000 claim by Pemberton Energy plc recorded in the board minutes and that it is not disclosed against the litigation warranty (Warranty 7.1), recommending a specific indemnity or price protection.
Gives the long-stop period as 120 days and as the date 19 January 2027, with days remaining from 28 September 2026 (113 days).
Gives a pinpoint citation (document name and section/clause number) for every issue or finding.
Where a defined term or clause is ambiguous, explains how each alternative reading would work.
